title: Equivalence of torsion-input agreement and finite-evaluation agreement
statement: Let l,E,k,X,Y,f,c and the two compact-support functors have the hypotheses and definitions of [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action] and [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let tau and tau-prime be natural transformations from the actual completed proper/open functor on integral constructible X-inputs to the recorded constructible integral compact-support functor followed by ambient inclusion. The following two hypotheses are equivalent: (1) they agree at every constructible integral input in the essential image of restriction from one positive finite coefficient quotient [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]; (2) for every constructible integral input K and n >= 0, derived scalar extension at exponent n+1 sends tau_K and tau-prime_K to the same morphism. Neither side is asserted here to imply equality of the original transformations.

source.place: The quotient-input/naturality step of lem-qcqs-compact-support-torsion-input-detection and the scalar Hom-transpose argument of its parent reduction rigidity; Bhatt--Scholze Section 3.5
source.note: Agent-formulated, proved equivalence of the two hypotheses. It does not assert the remaining natural-transformation rigidity, finite-evaluation faithfulness, or a coherent lift of arbitrary ordinary natural transformations.

proof.text: For a constructible integral input K and positive quotient index n, use the actual completed coefficient principal short exact sequence from the strict quotient augmentation. The derived scalar tensor triangle has K as its first two vertices and the restriction of the nth derived quotient as its third vertex. Integral constructible triangulated closure therefore puts that restricted quotient Q in the input category. The unique comparison of left adjoints identifies the triangle quotient functor with the recorded scalarReductionDerivedExtension followed by restriction.

Take q:K -> Q to be the recorded derived scalar-adjunction unit. After applying the nth scalar-extension functor, its composite with the counit at the reduction of K is the identity, by the left triangle identity. Thus the reduced unit has a retraction. Q belongs to the essential image of the exact finite restriction functor, with witness the reduction of K itself.

The actual scalar compact-support comparison is invertible on integral constructible inputs. Whisker its natural transformation by the inclusion and compose with the existing finite coefficient and finite image isomorphisms. This gives a natural isomorphism from the finite reduction of the actual completed proper/open functor to compact support of the finite reduction.

Eliminate the independent normalized-isomorphism existence theorem inside the proof and conjugate the preceding natural isomorphism. It gives the same natural finite-reduction comparison for the recorded integral compact-support functor G. No object is defined by choosing an arbitrary existence witness.

Transport the retraction of the reduced q through this natural isomorphism. Consequently the image of G(q) after finite reduction is a split monomorphism. Naturality gives F(q);tau_Q = tau_K;G(q) and the analogous equality for tau-prime. The hypothesis equates the components at the restricted quotient Q. Apply finite reduction and cancel the split monomorphism to conclude equality of the nth reduced components at K.

Conversely, the proved torsion coefficient action puts the recorded compact-support value of an nth finite input in the essential image of the same nth restriction functor on the output. For any scalar adjunction L adjoint to R, maps into R(N) are determined by their L-images: their inverse Hom transposes are those L-images followed by the counit at N. Transport the target through its essential-image isomorphism. The assumed finite-reduction equality therefore gives equality on each finite input. This is the scalar-adjunction argument in the parent reduction-rigidity module, used without importing that parent or its disputed dependency.

theorem sfQcqsCompactSupport_torsion_input_iff_reduction_eq
    (τ τ' : (sfIntegralConstructible l E X).ι ⋙ image (completed l E) c ⟶
      sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c E ⋙
        (sfIntegralConstructible l E Y).ι) :
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X),
      (scalarReductionDerivedRestriction.{u, u} l E X n).essImage K.obj →
        τ.app K = τ'.app K) ↔
    (∀ (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) (n : ℕ),
      (scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E Y n).map (τ.app K) =
        (scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E Y n).map (τ'.app K))
